oneliner.t: Republican from Monrovia who has represented the Huntsville-based 5th District since 2023 after 27 years on the Madison County Commission (chairman 2012–2023); unopposed for renomination in 2026, he faces Democrat Andrew Sneed.

profile.residence: Monrovia / Madison County, AL (not stated directly in sources reviewed)

upbringing.t: Strong is the son of Horace N. Strong, a founding member of the Monrovia Fire-Rescue Department, and Judy Vaughn Strong. He began as a volunteer firefighter at 13, graduated from Sparkman High School in 1988, holds an EMT license from the University of Alabama in Huntsville, and earned a B.S. in business administration from Athens State University. He worked as a first responder and 911 dispatcher for HEMSI and Huntsville Med-Flight, in public relations at First Alabama Bank and as a sales representative for Solvay before his 1996 election to the county commission. He married Laura Toney in 1999; they have two children. (Single source: Wikipedia; not independently corroborated in this pass.)

career.role: Volunteer firefighter; later first responder / 911 dispatcher

claims.claim: In the 2022 runoff, accused opponent Casey Wardynski of improper conduct tied to a school contract.

said.where: 2022 GOP runoff campaign (as reported by Wikipedia)

record.t: The underlying contract records were not reviewed; Wardynski disputed it.

claims.claim: Attributed differences in county fire funding (questioned by three volunteer fire chiefs in 2019) to property-tax levels, not favoritism toward Monrovia.
claims.short: Fire funding tied to tax levels

said.where: response to fire chiefs (as reported by Wikipedia)

record.t: County fire-district tax records were not reviewed.

claims.claim: Campaign said Strong keeps a strong financial position over each of his prospective opponents.

said.where: Strong campaign statement to Axios Huntsville

record.t: Per Axios, citing FEC filings at the end of 2025: Strong had about $1.07 million cash on hand in his campaign account, plus more than $70,000 in the Strong Victory Fund. Sneed had $204,553, and the other Democrats had raised $23,000 or less.

claims.claim: Campaign said that once the Strong Victory Fund joint account is counted, he outraised all opponents.

said.where: Strong campaign statement to Axios Huntsville

record.t: The statement answered reports that Sneed had outraised Strong in Q4 2025. Axios gives Strong's total for all of 2025 ($833,080, which is far above any opponent) and $80,000 raised by the joint fund in Oct–Nov 2025. It does not give the Q4 totals for either candidate, and the FEC filings tab did not load, so the Q4 comparison could not be checked.

entries.t: Voted Nay on the Fiscal Responsibility Act.
Voted Yea on H.R. 1, which included a $5 trillion debt-limit increase.
Voted Nay on H.R. 8035, the $60 billion Ukraine Security Supplemental.
Co-sponsored Rep. Eric Burlison's bill recognizing personhood from conception.
As commission chairman, approved moving a Confederate monument; the Attorney General sued under the Alabama Memorial Preservation Act and the county commission paid a $25,000 fine.
